thread:
maria: ran a quick A100 vs H100 pass for mistral-13b (q4_0) comparing cold-start (empty KV, first request) vs warmed (after steady 60s traffic). uploading plots: https://perf/reports/3943210000
perf-bot: run 3943210000 finished. summary attached.
zach: nice — what's the instance config + batch? :eyes:
maria: A100: p4d-like equiv (1xA100-80GB), H100: 1xH100-80GB. batch=1 decode only, prefill tokens=512, decode tokens=128. q=4_0 quant. region=us-west1 and eu-west1.
anya: what's the headline? tokens/sec and p99 latencies?
maria: H100 decode tokens/sec ~ 5.8k, A100 ~ 4.6k (batch=1). Prefill+decode p99: H100 215ms, A100 280ms on us-west1. Cold-start adds ~120ms on H100, ~200ms on A100 due to KV allocation and kernel warmup.
zach: that's a big cold delta. any kernel fallback noise? maybe we hit a new cuBLAS path on A100.
maria: saw a kernel fallthrough in logs: 'fallback kernel=matmul_small->generic_sgemm' for short-seq prefill on A100. H100 used fast-attn kernel consistently.
kevin: how are you computing $/1M tokens? include prefill amortization?
maria: yes — amortized prefill over session length 1k tokens. numbers: H100 $/1M tokens = $46.3, A100 = $55.8 (decode+prefill amortized). raw decode-only cost delta smaller: H100 $/1M = $38.1 vs A100 $/1M = $44.0.
anya: did you try increasing batch to 2 or 4? how does latency vs dollars trade?
maria: batch=2 raises tokens/sec ~+20% and increases p99 by ~15ms. batch=4 gives +40% tokens/sec but p99 +40ms (not great for low-latency apps). For throughput workloads, H100 still 20–25% cheaper per token.
zach: region differences?
maria: eu-west1 had ~8% higher p99 vs us-west1 due to cooler thermal profiles on our H100 pools; interestingly A100 had 3% higher p99 in eu-west1. thermal telemetry attached.
kevin: any model-quality diffs post-quant? same generations?
maria: no regressions detected on our eval set (BLEU/ROUGE/bertscore stable). ran 1k prompts.
anya: next steps?
maria: open PR with kernel pin for A100 to force fast-sgemm path for short-seq prefill, and schedule a longer 24h run to measure steady-state cost. will also try q8x4 for 13B and post results.
zach: :thumbsup:
kevin: thanks for the writeup, can you attach the CSV with raw samples?
maria: added CSV + small plot images to the perf report link.
perf-bot: artifact uploaded: /artifacts/3943210000/maria/mistral13b-warm-cold.zip
